clue.text: Range of tea now stocked

parts.note: char or cha is British slang for tea
goods now stocked are in, available in the shop

explanation.surface: A shop announcing that its new line of teas has just arrived on the shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' looks like a product range of teas, but it is the definition: a range of mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain of mountains is a range, a connected series of peaks.

clue.text: Ordered notice to be marked secret at the present time

parts.note: documents marked secret are classified
AD, anno domini, labels dates in the present era

explanation.surface: An official order that some notice be stamped secret from now on.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is apt twice over: a classified ad is a notice placed to order, and its first word also means secret.
explanation.definitionFit: A small newspaper advertisement is placed by order, paid for by the advertiser, so it is an ordered notice.

clue.text: See ritual reproduced on holiday

indicators.note: something reproduced is made again, here in a new arrangement of its letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tourist watching a local ceremony re-enacted while away on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on holiday has free time, with no work to be done, which is being unhurried and free.

clue.text: Irish girl picking up most important husband

indicators.note: in a down entry, picking something up lifts it, so the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: main means chief or most important
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: An Irish girl chooses the best husband available.
explanation.walkthrough: Niamh, said 'Neeve', is a common Irish girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Niamh is a traditional Irish female given name, from a goddess in Irish mythology.

clue.text: Ballet is out of place in old prison

indicators.note: letters out of place have been moved from their positions, so they must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ballet performance feels incongruous staged inside a former jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the Paris fortress used as a prison, stormed in 1789 at the start of the French Revolution.

clue.text: American friend becoming heartless, organising finances

indicators.note: a thing without a heart has lost its centre, so the middle letter goes

parts.note: bud is American slang for a friend
getting means becoming, as in getting old

explanation.surface: An American pal turns cold and starts managing the money.
explanation.walkthrough: GETTING loses one of its central Ts to give GETING.
explanation.definitionFit: Budgeting is planning how money will be spent, which is organising one's finances.

clue.text: Hazardous weather in south today

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
today, in the sense of at present, is now

explanation.surface: A forecast warning of dangerous conditions in the south today.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowfall is a kind of weather that can make roads and travel dangerous.

clue.text: Contract for one new set of teeth

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
N is a standard abbreviation for new
a denture is a set of false teeth

explanation.surface: A dental agreement for fitting someone with new false teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: An indenture is a formal legal agreement, especially one binding an apprentice to a master.

clue.text: In which cyclist may be a little painfully crashing

indicators.note: a little of something is only a small part of it, here a short run of letters across two words

parts.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A cyclist in a crash who comes off a little painfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is the stretchy synthetic fabric of the tight clothing cyclists typically wear.

clue.text: Everyone help empty the cabins

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a call for every available person to pitch in
second meaning: on a ship, the order that brings every sailor up from below

explanation.surface: A call for everyone to pitch in and clear out the cabins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabins' suggests a cleaning job, but these are a ship's cabins, emptied when the whole crew is summoned on top.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a naval order summoning the entire crew to work, and now means any emergency call for every available person.

clue.text: Tasty oranges are rotten, believe it or not

indicators.note: rotten fruit has broken down, so these letters fall apart and are rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Surprisingly, the delicious oranges have gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are interjections introducing a surprising fact the listener may find hard to credit.

clue.text: Insulted slim newspaper person

parts.note: slight means slender or slim
ED is short for editor, who runs a newspaper

explanation.surface: A thin journalist was insulted by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To slight someone is to snub or treat them with disrespect, so a slighted person has been insulted.

clue.text: Complete discretion after heart of business exposed

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only its middle letters are kept
something exposed has had its covering stripped away, leaving only the inner part

parts.note: the two central letters of the word
tact is discretion in dealing with people

explanation.surface: Total confidentiality, now that the core of a firm's dealings has been revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places TACT after the other piece, so the selected letters lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intact is whole and undamaged, so it is complete.

clue.text: Say you must interrupt caressing abandoned child

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks into the middle of something else

parts.note: fondling means caressing

indicators.note: say asks for the next word as it is pronounced, by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: the letter U is pronounced like the word you

explanation.surface: Telling someone to stop the petting and pay attention to a neglected child.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundling is an infant found after being deserted by its parents.

clue.text: Resolve, may we infer, to encourage yours?

parts.note: deter is the opposite of encourage
mine is the opposite of yours

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what spurring on your own side might imply.
explanation.walkthrough: Each piece is the opposite of its clue word; 'may we infer' and the question mark warn that the solver must flip the meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine is to settle or decide firmly, the same as to resolve.

clue.text: Go visiting and buy some drinks

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to travel about, calling on many people
second meaning: to purchase a round, drinks for everyone in a group at the pub

explanation.surface: A night of calling on friends and standing them drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British pub, buying a round means paying for a drink for everyone in your group.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to move about socially, and split as get a round it means to purchase a set of pub drinks.

clue.text: Invisible, such violet light

parts.note: surface reading: a description of a faint, unseeable purple glow
setter's reading: the word that, put before violet, names the light beyond the visible spectrum

explanation.surface: A description of a purple glow that cannot be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the prefix that turns violet into the name of radiation past the visible violet end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultraviolet radiation lies beyond the visible spectrum, so it is invisible to the human eye.

clue.text: Competitor in camp combining with three

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another, here the rival inside the shelter

parts.note: a tent is a camp shelter
a rival is a competitor

explanation.surface: A competitor at a camp who teams up with three others.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is chemistry: an atom's valency is how many bonds it forms.
explanation.definitionFit: A trivalent atom has a valency of three, so it bonds with three other atoms.

clue.text: Yet time for something to happen

parts.note: even can mean yet, as in even better
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Still waiting for the moment when something finally happens.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occurrence, a thing that takes place.

clue.text: Crowd finally attending a music drama

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
taken as written
The Ring is Wagner's cycle of four operas, which he called music dramas

explanation.surface: A crowd at last turns up to an opera performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Wagner called his operas music dramas, and The Ring is the most famous.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering is a group of people come together, a crowd.

clue.text: Busy couple in lifeboat

indicators.note: in puts one thing inside another, here the pair inside the boat

parts.note: Noah's ark was the boat that saved life from the flood
a couple is two

explanation.surface: A pair of crew members occupied on a lifeboat.
explanation.walkthrough: The animals boarded the ark two by two, which suits the couple inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at work is occupied with their job, so busy.

clue.text: Leaving hospital, we have to follow winding route

indicators.note: the hospital abbreviation leaving means that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; H, for hospital, then departs

explanation.surface: After being discharged, we have a long meandering journey home.
explanation.definitionFit: To weave is to move by twisting and turning, as through traffic, following a zigzag course.

clue.text: Expecting such a significant pause?

definitions.note: describes the pause; the answer is the adjective applied to it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the adjective in the phrase for a pause full of meaning

explanation.surface: Asks whether a meaningful silence hints at a coming baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause full of unspoken meaning is a pregnant pause, and expecting a baby is being pregnant.

clue.text: Getting name into network is drudgery

indicators.note: into places one thing inside another, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a grid is a network, as of lines or power cables
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Getting a name recognised within a professional network is hard slog.
explanation.definitionFit: A grind is tedious, hard work, the same as drudgery.

clue.text: Rely on changing instrument

indicators.note: changing alters the word, here the order of its letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Depend on swapping to a different instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyre is a stringed instrument like a small harp, played in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Relatively profitable organisation?

parts.note: surface reading: a company that makes a moderate profit
setter's reading: run by relatives, a firm owned and staffed by one household

explanation.surface: A company that makes a fair amount of money, comparatively speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relatively' seems to mean comparatively, but it is read as by relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial firm owned and run by members of one household is a profit-making organisation of relatives.

clue.text: As rector, always aim to be called this

definitions.text: As rector, always aim to be called this

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rector
ever means always, as in for ever
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: Advice to a clergyman on the title he should strive for.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a rector is addressed by the title the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverend is the honorific title of a member of the clergy, used for a rector.

clue.text: Scatterbrained, as Dorothy may be called

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slightly mad or absent-minded
second meaning: a familiar pet form of the name Dorothy

explanation.surface: A forgetful woman earns an affectionate nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotty is informal for eccentric or feather-brained, and it is also a short form of the given name Dorothy.
